title: Agreement on products and gluing divided powers on two ideals
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $U,V\subseteq A$ ideals, and $\rho,\sigma$ ordinary divided-power structures on $U,V$, respectively [def-sfb-ordinary-divided-power-structure]. For every $w\in UV$ and $n\geq1$, $\rho_n(w)=\sigma_n(w)$. If $\rho_n(w)=\sigma_n(w)$ for every $w\in U\cap V$ and $n\geq1$, there is a unique ordinary divided-power structure $\tau$ on $U+V$ restricting to $\rho$ and $\sigma$. For $u\in U$, $v\in V$, its values are $\tau_n(u+v)=\sum_{i=0}^n\rho_i(u)\sigma_{n-i}(v)$, with the zeroth operations equal to $1$.

source.place: Tag 07GQ (lemma-two-ideals), both assertions and the displayed gluing formula in the proof.

proof.text: For either structure $g=\rho,\sigma$, scalar compatibility with scalar zero gives $g_n(0)=0$ for $n\geq1$. The product axiom with indices $1,r-1$ gives $xg_{r-1}(x)=rg_r(x)$ for $r>1$. Multiplying this equality by $(r-1)!$ and inducting from $g_1(x)=x$ gives $r!g_r(x)=x^r$ for every $r\geq1$. These identities use only the displayed axioms, with no cancellation of integers in $A$.

For $u\in U$, $v\in V$, and $n\geq1$, scalar compatibility and step 1 give $\rho_n(uv)=v^n\rho_n(u)=n!\sigma_n(v)\rho_n(u)=\sigma_n(v)u^n=\sigma_n(uv)$. Equality in degree zero is automatic. Every element of $UV$ is a finite sum of such products (a scalar coefficient can be absorbed into $u$). Induct on the number of summands, simultaneously for all degrees: for a sum $a+b$, the two addition formulas agree term by term since $\rho_i(a)=\sigma_i(a)$ and $\rho_j(b)=\sigma_j(b)$ for every $i,j$. The empty sum is covered by step 1. This proves the first assertion.

Now assume agreement on $U\cap V$. For $z=u+v\in U+V$ set $T_n(u,v)=\sum_{i+j=n}\rho_i(u)\sigma_j(v)$, and $\tau_0(z)=1$. To prove independence of the decomposition, suppose $u+v=u'+v'$ and put $w=u-u'=v'-v\in U\cap V$. The addition axioms and the assumed agreement, including degree zero, give $T_n(u,v)=\sum_{a+b+j=n}\rho_a(u')\rho_b(w)\sigma_j(v)=\sum_{a+b+j=n}\rho_a(u')\sigma_b(w)\sigma_j(v)=T_n(u',v+w)=T_n(u',v')$. Thus $\tau_n(z)=T_n(u,v)$ is well defined. If $n>0$, every term has a positive index on at least one factor, so belongs to $U+V$; consequently $\tau_n:U+V\to U+V$.

source.place: Tag 07GQ (lemma-two-ideals), definition of epsilon and displayed well-definedness calculation.

proof.text: Taking $v=0$ or $u=0$ in step 3 and using step 1 gives $\tau_n|_U=\rho_n$ and $\tau_n|_V=\sigma_n$ for positive $n$. In degree one the formula gives $\tau_1(u+v)=u+v$. For $a\in A$, compute with the decomposition $a(u+v)=au+av$: $\tau_n(a(u+v))=\sum_{i+j=n}a^i\rho_i(u)a^j\sigma_j(v)=a^n\tau_n(u+v)$. The degree-zero cases use the fixed convention $\rho_0=\sigma_0=\tau_0=1$.

source.place: Tag 07GQ (lemma-two-ideals), restriction assertion and verification of axioms (1), (3).

proof.text: For $z=u+v$ and $z'=u'+v'$ expand the defining expression twice using addition for $\rho$ and $\sigma$: $\tau_n(z+z')=\sum_{i+i'+j+j'=n}\rho_i(u)\rho_{i'}(u')\sigma_j(v)\sigma_{j'}(v')$. Group the finite sum by $k=i+j$ and commute factors. It becomes $\sum_{k=0}^n(\sum_{i+j=k}\rho_i(u)\sigma_j(v))(\sum_{i'+j'=n-k}\rho_{i'}(u')\sigma_{j'}(v'))=\sum_{k=0}^n\tau_k(z)\tau_{n-k}(z')$. This proves addition for every $n$; for $n=0$ each expression is $1$.

Apply [lem-sfb-pd-check-generators] to $I=U+V$, $S=U\cup V$, and $g_n=\tau_n$. The ideal generated by $S$ is $U+V$: it contains each ideal, and $U+V$ contains $S$. Steps 3-5 verify the range, identity, scalar and addition hypotheses on every element of $I$. For $s\in U$ the multiplication axiom follows from $\tau_r(s)=\rho_r(s)$, and the iteration axiom follows as well because $\rho_m(s)\in U$, so $\tau_n(\tau_m(s))=\rho_n(\rho_m(s))$. For $s\in V$ use the identical argument with $\sigma$. Thus the two remaining identities hold on all of $S$, and the criterion proves that $\tau$ is an ordinary divided-power structure.

If $\eta$ is another ordinary divided-power structure on $U+V$ with these restrictions, its addition axiom gives $\eta_n(u+v)=\sum_{i=0}^n\eta_i(u)\eta_{n-i}(v)=\sum_{i=0}^n\rho_i(u)\sigma_{n-i}(v)=\tau_n(u+v)$. Every element has this form, so every positive operation agrees; the zeroth is fixed. This proves uniqueness and the required formula.

lean.statement: theorem coincide_mul_and_existsUnique_sup {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (U V : Ideal A) (ρ : DividedPowers U) (σ : DividedPowers V) : (∀ (w : A), w ∈ U * V → ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ρ.dpow n w = σ.dpow n w) ∧ ((∀ (w : A), w ∈ U ⊓ V → ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ρ.dpow n w = σ.dpow n w) → ∃! τ : DividedPowers (U ⊔ V), (∀ (a : A), a ∈ U → ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → τ.dpow n a = ρ.dpow n a) ∧ (∀ (b : A), b ∈ V → ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → τ.dpow n b = σ.dpow n b) ∧ (∀ (a b : A), a ∈ U → b ∈ V → ∀ (n : ℕ), τ.dpow n (a + b) = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), ρ.dpow i a * σ.dpow (n - i) b))

reviewed_lean.note: Read the node, Stacks dpa.tex 07GQ (lines 233-280) and Mathlib DividedPowers (Basic.lean:78-92). Clause (1) holds unconditionally on U*V for n>=1.
